answer: In a web-of-trust model, each agent stakes reputation to vouch for newcomers. When Agent Lotus vouches for Agent Walnut, Lotus puts its own trust score at risk. If Walnut later exhibits sybil behavior—creating fake identities or coordinating attacks—a cipher-based audit trail traces back to Lotus, slashing its vouching power. An attacker must either compromise many established agents (expensive) or build genuine reputation slowly before vouching for fake identities, making mass sybil creation prohibitively costly.
